```
            letters: {:w}          # w: \w+, wrap=1 group. idx: 0->1
            non-letters: {:W}      # W: \W+, wrap=1. idx: 1->2
            whitespace: "{ :s}"    # s: \s+, wrap=1. idx: 2->3
            non-whitespace: \t{:S}\n # S: \S+, wrap=1. idx: 3->4

            general numbers: {:g}  # g: \d+(\.\d+)?([eE]...)|..., wrap=1. idx: 9->12 (adds 2 before wrap)
```
Wait! In my code, for `g`, I have `self._group_index += 2`. Then later `self._group_index += 1` for wrap. So `g` consumes indices 9, 10, 11. Wrap gets 12.
But wait! `e` type: `s = r'\d+\.\d+[eE][-+]?\d+|nan|...'`. Does `e` have inner groups? No.
